problem: The sentence is broken: "In thermal equilibrium N2/N1 = exp(−hf/kT)  N1, an inverted population." Part of the argument (that N2 < N1 at equilibrium, and that inversion means N2 > N1) has dropped out, so the reader cannot follow why pumping is needed.
fix: In thermal equilibrium N2/N1 = exp(−hf/kT) < 1, so N2 < N1 and absorption dominates. Laser action needs N2 > N1, an inverted population. That is why a laser needs pumping; see laser action.

problem: "it happens after τ_sp" reads as if the atom waits exactly τ_sp before dropping. τ_sp is only the average delay; single atoms decay at random times.
fix: Spontaneous emission does not need a second photon; it happens at a random time whose average is τ_sp.

problem: Two symbols are used without definition: ρ(f), the spectral energy density, and k, T in exp(−hf/kT). A student cannot check units.
fix: State: ρ(f) is the energy density per unit frequency in J m⁻³ Hz⁻¹; k = 1.38×10⁻²³ J/K is Boltzmann's constant; T is temperature in kelvin.
